qwen.ref_text: On the battlefield, four players with monster-like strength appeared. Each of the players had already destroyed their colonies. These players were so equally strong, they created a four-way deadlock.

lines: Lecture eight. The Ant System. This is how ants build tours, and how trails learn.
Each iteration has three steps. Step one puts the ants on random towns.
Step 1: put the ants on random towns.
Step two. Every ant builds a whole tour.
Step 2: every ant builds a whole tour.
Step three. The roads the ants used get thicker.
Step 3: roads the ants used get thicker.
Then the loop repeats. The ants forget, but the trails remember.
Repeat until done. Ants forget; trails remember.
One ant starts on town T, and that town goes on its tabu list.
Its start town goes on the tabu list.
At each step, it picks a town that is still allowed.
It picks a town that is still allowed.
A town on the tabu list is never picked again.
A visited town is never picked again.
When nothing is allowed, the ant goes home. The tour is seventy-four kilometres long.
Back home: tour length 74 km.
For the next tour, the tabu list starts empty.
Next tour: the tabu list starts empty.
At a town, the ant scores each road.
Each road gets a score.
Closeness, or the heuristic, is one over the distance, so nearer is higher.
Closeness (heuristic) is 1 over distance.
The score is the trail times the closeness.
Score: trail times closeness.
A village already visited scores zero, however strong its trail.
A visited town scores zero.
Each score's share of the total is its chance. Here that is twenty, forty, forty and zero percent.
Each score's share of the total is its chance.
The ant draws a random number between zero and one.
The ant draws a random number.
The slice it lands in wins. Zero point three one falls in the Birch slice.
The slice it lands in wins.
Unlikely roads can still win. Zero point zero eight lands in the small Ash slice.
Unlikely roads can still win.
Now the rule gets two dials. The score is trail to the power alpha, times closeness to the power beta.
Same rule as before, with two dials.
Alpha is trust in the trail. Beta is trust in closeness.
Alpha trusts the trail; beta, closeness.
Alpha zero and beta three ignores the trail, and favours the nearest village, with eighty-two percent.
Alpha 0, beta 3: the nearest is favoured.
Alpha three and beta zero ignores distance, and favours the strongest trail.
Alpha 3, beta 0: the strongest trail is favoured.
Take one road, with a trail of four.
This road carries a trail of 4.
First, evaporation. Half fades away, which leaves two.
Evaporation: half of it fades.
Then each ant on the road adds Q over its tour length. With Q at one hundred, tours of twenty-five, fifty and a hundred kilometres add four, two and one.
Each ant that used it adds Q over its tour length.
Shorter tours leave more trail.
Shorter tours leave more.
The new trail is two plus seven, which is nine.
New trail: 2 + 7 = 9.
A colony of ten ants runs on ten villages. At first the trails are thin and equal.
At first the trails are thin and equal.
Short tours leave more trail.
Short tours leave more trail.
So more ants follow that trail.
So more ants follow that trail.
More ants add more trail, so it snowballs.
More ants, more trail: it snowballs.
In fourteen iterations, the share of trail on the best tour climbs from forty to a hundred percent.
The colony settles on one short tour.
Six ants have finished. The variants differ in which of them add trail.
Six ants finish. Which of them add trail?
In the Ant System, all ants add trail.
Ant System: all ants add trail.
In elitist rank, only the best three do.
Elitist rank: only the best 3.
In the Max-Min style, only the best one does.
Max-Min style: only the best 1.
Fewer depositors pile more trail onto the best tour. Its share rises from fifty-three to ninety, then ninety-seven percent.
Fewer depositors pile trail on the best tour.
But more runs end on a poor tour: three, five, then seventeen out of forty.
But more runs end on a poor tour.
Ants are not only for tours. Here is a print shop, with five jobs and one press.
A print shop: five jobs, one press.
The ant picks a job by the same rule as before.
The ant picks a job by the same rule.
It picks one job at a time, never twice.
It picks one job at a time, never twice.
The path is the schedule. Lateness is the finish time minus the due time.
Lateness: finish time minus due time.
On average, a job is fifty-four minutes late, and the worst is seventy.
Average 54 minutes late, worst 70.
The loop is place, build, update, and repeat.
Score each road as trail times closeness, then draw by chance.
Update by evaporating, then adding Q over the tour length.
